pearson: Pauling file includes both Co2Si (C37) and PbCl2 (C23) as structure types. Co2Si is sometimes called anti-PbCl2. The structures differ in a/b ratio. For 1.25 < a/b < 1.40 we have Co2Si and for 1.50 < a/b < 1.90 we have PbCl2. However, there is not really a clear distinction; e.g. AuTm2 with a/b=1.44 is listed as Co2Si type and AuYb2 with a/b=1.71 (if correct) is listed as PbCl2 type. This makes no sense. I list both under Co2Si with SB C37. HgCl2 with SB C25 also has the same space group and Wyckoff positions.

pearson: The alpha-Sm structure has been assigned the Strukturbericht C19 that originally was assigned to CdCl2, indicating that alpha-Sm and CdCl2 have the same structure. This does not seem approprite. Alpha-Sm is a stacking variant of close packed atom layers, belonging to the family fcc, hcp and dhcp, whereas CdCl2 is a strongly ordered ionic structure with Cl forming a close packed structure and Cd as ordered interstitials. The C19 Strukturbericht will be removed from alpha-Sm.

prototype: This table contains phases both from binary systems (SGTE binary collection) and higher order systems, mostly ternary systems that I have processed. Often it seems obvious that several compounds (e.g. with different rare earths) should be modelled as a single phase, but it turns out to be very difficult to draw the line once one starts to consider which compounds should be modelled as a single phase.
